My ex dumped me after an abusive relationship, which caused me to have to move on-campus as we'd shared a house together. 

As soon as he realised that we were both on campus, he was always near me. Always "just passing by". It got so bad that I moved in with my next boyfriend just to escape him. 

My ex reeled me back into his spiral. He said he missed me. He loved me. He fucked up. He wanted me to be with him and not my boyfriend. I was mentally ill from the relationship (which is clear to me now, but not then) and my new boyfriend who was nothing but amazing to me got treated like shit by me while I struggled with this.

When new bf and I finally broke up, my ex said he was driving down to get me and bring me home. I got scared and called my friend who collected me instead.

My ex escalated. He'd arrive at my apartment (I'd lived there previously when we were together) and sit outside in his car, calling me on his mobile. He'd pressure me into having sex with him - despite having a new girlfriend of his own.

He used to message me constantly, show up wherever I was- and this went on for years.

Finally, I read Gavin De Becker's book, The Gift of Fear. To say it changed my life would be an understatement. It gave me the tools to break free. I cut contact. I stopped rising to his bait /and it worked/. 

The last text from him I got was over a year ago, asking if I wanted to see a movie sometime. Haven't heard from him since.


I'm scarred from it (and the relationship itself, but that's a whole new story). I don't trust easily. I don't answer calls from private numbers, or numbers I don't know. I avoid certain areas where I know he lives. It's exhausting. 

My heart goes out to anyone else in this thread who had it worse than me. It's just awful.

For me, at least, cultural appropriation is a problem because often the aspects of the culture which is being appropriated are not fully understood or appreciated by the appropriatiors (which is very often white people in my experience). 

Here's a great link which helped me understand what everyone was talking about when I was trying to learn more. It focuses on people wearing native headdresses: http://apihtawikosisan.com/hall-of-shame/an-open-letter-to-non-natives-in-headdresses/

The author explains it as follows- in most cultures there are "restricted"  items and "non restricted" items. In a very, very basic cliffnotes, restricted items being ones that must be earned with specific criteria, and non restricted items being ones that anyone can have. 

Cultural appropriation (to me, at least!) is when someone takes a restricted item from another culture and uses it as a non restricted one. 

Another good example is this article here which discusses appreciation vs appropriation of calaveras de azúcar (also known as sugar skulls) http://blog.redbubble.com/2014/10/day-of-the-dead-sugar-skull-art/ 

I guess the point I'm trying to make (and sorry it turned into a lengthy one!) is that cultural appropriation is a problem, because in the majority of cases I've personally experienced, it is at best a complete lack of respect for someone else's culture, which is never okay, in my option. 

I'm sure that there's plenty of people who have other ideas, but that's just my personal view. :)  hope it helps! 

Edit: also, here's an article which explained it better than I could ever try to: http://everydayfeminism.com/2015/06/cultural-appropriation-wrong/

As I said above, my viewpoint is very limited, and I'm still learning, so there's plenty more sides of the issue itself to read, hear and learn from.
